definition: Turbulent means characterized by conflict, disorder, or sudden violent change; unsettled and disorderly.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word turbulent. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know turbulent should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Below the falls the river turned turbulent, all churning white water and flying spray.
An unsettled situation is uneasy and shifting; a turbulent one is churning with open conflict and disorder.
Explosive is stronger than turbulent — the disorder is no longer just churning, it is bursting into outright violence.

Stormy borrows the weather to describe outbursts — a stormy meeting, a stormy marriage — where anger keeps breaking like thunder. Turbulent covers disorder and sudden change whether or not anyone is angry: a turbulent year of swings and reversals can pass without a single raised voice.

Tumultuous means loud, disorderly, and confused — the roar of a crowd — and it can even be joyful: a tumultuous welcome, tumultuous applause. Turbulent is never celebratory; it means churning conflict and instability. A tumultuous crowd might be cheering; a turbulent one is close to riot.

Unstable means likely to shift or collapse suddenly — it is about what might happen, a weakness waiting under load. Turbulent is about what is happening: disorder actively churning, prices lurching, factions fighting. An unstable government has not fallen yet; a turbulent one is already in upheaval.

It was a turbulent year for the stock market: prices soared in the spring, crashed in June, and swung wildly all autumn.
The market didn't move smoothly — it lurched through sudden, violent changes with no stability anywhere.
Turbulent describes exactly that kind of unsettled, disorderly period, whether in water, weather, politics, or finance.

Turbulent works literally for air and water (a turbulent river, turbulent skies — on a flight you feel the related noun turbulence) and figuratively for periods, relationships, and emotions: a turbulent decade, a turbulent friendship, turbulent feelings.
